rows.grounds: compound pīṭha-tāra; subject of the prescribed measurement
compound tri-bhāga-eka; specifies a measure of one third
compound go-mukha-dīrgha; indicates length equal to the spout

items.question: What proportional width and length are prescribed for the pedestal and its spout?
premises: The pedestal width is the measured element under specification.
Its width is defined as one third part.
Its length is defined as equal to the cow-mouth spout.
items.inference: The pedestal width is prescribed as one third, with a length equal to the spout.
uncertainties: The exact referent of tribhāgaikaṃ as one third of which whole is not explicit in this verse alone.
items.plain_english: The width of the pedestal is stated to be one third, and its length is said to be equal to that of the cow-mouth spout.
